surfaces.stdout:
module std/iterator

# The sources are classes, as the other library's are: an adaptor keeps
# its source by value, and a struct source was copied into it, so
# `it.first(2).to_a` and then `it.to_a` gave [1, 2] and [1, 2, 3, 4] where
# the other library gives [1, 2] and [3, 4]. Shared, the adaptor's pulls
# are the source's. An adaptor that keeps a count, a flag or a buffer is
# the source of whatever is built on it, so it is a class for the same
# reason: as a struct it was copied too, and `t = it.take(3)`,
# `t.first(2).to_a` and then `t.to_a` gave [3, 4, 5] where the other
# library gives [3], `each_cons` handed its first window out again and
# `step` and `with_index` restarted their strides and counts. An adaptor
# that keeps only its sources, a block or a size stays a struct: a copy of
# it pulls from the same place.
#
# Each type defines `next` once and its `impl` names only `Elem`, as
# `NumericStepIterator` (std/steppable) does: every adaptor carried the same
# `next` twice, once on the type and once in the `impl`.
pub class ArrayIterator(T)
  def initialize(array : Array(T))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class ChainIterator(I1, I2, T)
  def initialize(iter1 : I1, iter2 : I2)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub struct CompactMapIterator(I, T, U)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> U | ::Nil))
  def next : U | Stop
end

pub class ConsIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : Array(T) | Stop
end

pub class CycleIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class CycleNIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : T | Stop
end

# The source an endless range gets: it counts up by one from the beginning
# with no end, as an endless range does in the other library.
pub class EndlessRangeIterator(B)
  def initialize(current : B)
  def next : B
end

pub class EntryIterator(K, V)
  def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V))
  def next : Tuple(K, V) | Stop
end

pub class FlatMapIterator(I, T, U)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Array(U)))
  def next : U | Stop
end

pub trait Iterator
  type Elem
  def all?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  # Whether an element is truthy, which is what the other library's `any?`
  # answers: this said whether there was an element at all, so
  # `Iterator.of([false, false]).any?` was true. It pulls until it meets a
  # truthy element, and what it pulled is gone: an iterator is a pull, so a
  # predicate over one cannot be free. For a source with no `false` in it
  # that is one element. The block form below reads as much as it has to
  # and no more. Said here because a method spelled like a question that
  # quietly takes elements is the kind of thing a caller finds out from the
  # answer to the *next* question.
  def any? : Bool
  def any?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  def chain(other : O) : ChainIterator(self, O, Elem | O::Elem) forall O : Iterator
  def compact_map(&func : (Elem -> U | ::Nil)) : CompactMapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U
  def count : Int32
  def count(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Int32
  def cycle(n : Int32) : CycleNIterator(self, Elem)
  def cycle : CycleIterator(self, Elem)
  def each(& : (Elem -> Nil)) : Nil
  def each_cons(n : Int32) : ConsIterator(self, Elem)
  def each_slice(n : Int32) : SliceIterator(self, Elem)
  # Nil when nothing matched, which is what `Enumerable#find` and `Array#find`
  # answer: not finding is the ordinary outcome of a search, and a caller who
  # wants the panic writes `|| raise` as the prelude does. `first?`/`first`
  # below keeps its pair — an exhausted iterator has no first element, which
  # is a question with no answer.
  def find(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Elem | ::Nil
  def first(n : Int32) : TakeIterator(self, Elem)
  def first : Elem
  def first? : Elem | ::Nil
  def flat_map(&func : (Elem -> Array(U))) : FlatMapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U
  def map(&func : (Elem -> U)) : MapIterator(self, Elem, U) forall U
  def max : Elem where Elem : Comparable
  # The largest, or nil when there is none. `max?`/`max` is a real pair:
  # an empty source has no largest element, so the plain name raising is
  # the common case. This file keeps the same pair for `first?`/`first`,
  # and answers `find` with nil, where not finding is the ordinary outcome.
  def max? : Elem | ::Nil where Elem : Comparable
  def min : Elem where Elem : Comparable
  # And the same pair at the other end.
  def min? : Elem | ::Nil where Elem : Comparable
  abstract def next : Elem | Stop
  def none?(& : (Elem -> Bool)) : Bool
  # Convenience constructor for arrays.
  def self.of(array : Array(T)) : ArrayIterator(T) forall T
  # An endless range counts up for as long as it is pulled, as the other
  # library's does: `Iterator.of((1..)).first(3).to_a` was accepted here
  # and then refused from inside `RangeIterator#next`, "expected argument
  # #1 to 'Int32#<' to be ... not Nil", a line of this file. A beginless
  # range has no first element to count from, and is refused at the call.
  def self.of(range : Range(B, Nil)) : EndlessRangeIterator(B) forall B
  def self.of(range : Range(Nil, E)) : Nil forall E
  def self.of(range : Range(B, E)) : RangeIterator(B, E) forall B, E
  def self.of_entries(hash : Hash(K, V)) : EntryIterator(K, V) forall K, V
  def self.of_keys(hash : Hash(K, V)) : KeyIterator(K, V) forall K, V
  def self.of_values(hash : Hash(K, V)) : ValueIterator(K, V) forall K, V
  def product : Elem where Elem : Num
  def reduce(initial : U, & : (U, Elem -> U)) : U forall U
  def reduce?(& : (Elem, Elem -> Elem)) : Elem | ::Nil
  def reject(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : RejectIterator(self, Elem)
  def select(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : SelectIterator(self, Elem)
  def size : Int32
  def skip(n : Int32) : SkipIterator(self, Elem)
  def skip_while(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : SkipWhileIterator(self, Elem)
  def step(n : Int32) : StepIterator(self, Elem)
  def sum : Elem where Elem : Num
  def take(n : Int32) : TakeIterator(self, Elem)
  def take_while(&func : (Elem -> Bool)) : TakeWhileIterator(self, Elem)
  def to_a : Array(Elem)
  def with_index(offset : Int32 = 0) : WithIndexIterator(self, Elem)
  def with_index(offset : Int32 = 0, & : (Elem, Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Bounded, as `Enumerable#zip` is (SPEC.md II.6 finding 6). Unbounded, a
  # zip with an array was refused from inside this file, "undefined
  # constant O::Elem" at the line below, and a chain with one from
  # `ChainIterator#next`; with `forall O : Iterator` the refusal names the
  # caller's line, the argument's type and `O`. A chain of two element
  # types yields either, as the other library's does: it was a return-type
  # error inside `ChainIterator`.
  def zip(other : O) : ZipIterator(self, Elem, O, O::Elem) forall O : Iterator
end

# The three views of a hash, in insertion order. Each takes its snapshot of
# the hash once, when built — `Hash#keys` and `Hash#values` allocate a fresh
# array per call, so asking per element was a copy of the table per step —
# and then walks that snapshot, so a hash that changes under the iterator
# does not change what it yields.
pub class KeyIterator(K, V)
  def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V))
  def next : K | Stop
end

pub struct MapIterator(I, T, U)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> U))
  def next : U | Stop
end

# Counts up by one from the range's beginning, the way the prelude's
# `Range#each` does, and stops at the end rather than stepping past it:
# on an inclusive range whose end is the type's largest value, the step
# after the last element would overflow.
pub class RangeIterator(B, E)
  def initialize(range : Range(B, E))
  def next : B | Stop
end

pub struct RejectIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub struct SelectIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class SkipIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class SkipWhileIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub struct SliceIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : Array(T) | Stop
end

pub class StepIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, by : Int32)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub struct Stop
  def initialize
end

pub class TakeIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, n : Int32)
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class TakeWhileIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, func : (T -> Bool))
  def next : T | Stop
end

pub class ValueIterator(K, V)
  def initialize(hash : Hash(K, V))
  def next : V | Stop
end

pub class WithIndexIterator(I, T)
  def initialize(iter : I, offset : Int32)
  def next : Tuple(T, Int32) | Stop
end

pub struct ZipIterator(I1, T1, I2, T2)
  def initialize(iter1 : I1, iter2 : I2)
  # Asks the second source only when the first has an element. Asking both
  # took one from the second each time the first had run out: after
  # `a.zip(b).to_a` with `a` = [1] and `b` = [10, 20, 30], `b.next`
  # answered 30 where the other library and Python's `zip` answer 20.
  def next : Tuple(T1, T2) | Stop
end

impl Iterator for EndlessRangeIterator(B) forall B
end

surfaces.stdout:
module std/json

# `derive serializable`, in a struct or class whose fields are written with
# their types: the type reads and writes itself as a JSON object, a key per
# field, named as the field is.
#
#     pub struct Coord
#       getter x : Float64
#       getter name : String
#       derive serializable
#     end
#
#     Coord.from_json(%({"x": 1.5, "name": "a"})).x   # => 1.5
#     coord.to_json                                   # => {"x":1.5,"name":"a"}
#
# A field's value is read and written as `JSON.read_value` and
# `JSON.write_value` read and write its type: the built-in values, an
# `Array` or `Hash(String, V)` of them, an `Any`, another serializable
# type. A key the type has no field for is passed over; a field with no
# key keeps its default when it is written with one, as does a field with
# a default whose key holds `null` where its type does not admit nil; a
# field with neither is refused by name unless its type admits `nil`,
# which it then holds. It is what the other library's `include
# JSON::Serializable` writes, and the derive runs once, in the type's own
# module (SPEC.md II.4), so a consumer calls the methods without the macro.
pub macro serializable(declaration)

# One JSON value of any kind, the result of `JSON.parse`. The `as_x` methods
# panic when the value is of another kind; the `as_x?` ones answer `nil`.
pub struct Any
  alias Type = Nil | Bool | Int64 | Float64 | String | Array(Any) | Hash(String, Any)
  # Equal when the values are: an integer equals the float with the same
  # value, arrays element by element, objects key by key in any order.
  def ==(other : Any) : Bool
  def [](index : Int32) : Any
  def [](key : String) : Any
  def []?(index : Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def []?(key : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def as_a : Array(Any)
  def as_a? : Array(Any) | ::Nil
  def as_bool : Bool
  def as_bool? : Bool | ::Nil
  # A float, or an integer read as one.
  def as_f : Float64
  def as_f? : Float64 | ::Nil
  def as_h : Hash(String, Any)
  def as_h? : Hash(String, Any) | ::Nil
  def as_i : Int32
  def as_i64 : Int64
  def as_i64? : Int64 | ::Nil
  def as_i? : Int32 | ::Nil
  def as_nil : Nil
  def as_s : String
  def as_s? : String | ::Nil
  def dig(key : String) : Any
  def dig(index : Int32) : Any
  def dig(k : String, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any
  def dig(idx : Int32, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any
  def dig?(key : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def dig?(index : Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def dig?(k : String, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def dig?(idx : Int32, *subkeys : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  protected def float_value? : Float64 | ::Nil
  # Consistent with `==`: a whole float hashes as the integer it equals, an
  # object's hash does not depend on the order its keys were written in.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize(raw : Type)
  def inspect : String
  # The kind of value this is, in the word a refusal uses: `null`, `bool`,
  # `integer`, `float`, `string`, `array` or `object`.
  def kind : String
  def self.new(val : Int32) : Any
  def raw : Type
  # How many elements an array or an object holds. A scalar has no size.
  def size : Int32
  def size? : Int32 | ::Nil
  def to_ascii_json : String
  def to_json : String
  def to_pretty_json(indent : String = "  ") : String
  # A string as itself and null as nothing, as `YAML::Any#to_s` and the
  # other library answer them; a number, a boolean or a collection as its
  # JSON text. A string was its JSON text too, so `"hello #{doc["name"]}"`
  # printed `hello "Ada"`, and null printed `null`.
  def to_s : String
end

# Writes a document one value at a time. `indent=` makes it pretty;
# `ascii_only=` escapes every non-ASCII code point.
pub class Builder
  def array(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  def ascii_only : Bool
  def ascii_only=(value : Bool) : Bool
  def bool(val : Bool) : Nil
  # Whether no value has been written yet.
  def empty? : Bool
  def end_array : Nil
  def end_object : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Any) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : String) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Int32) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Int64) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Float64) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Bool) : Nil
  def field(name : String, val : Nil) : Nil
  # A key; the value that follows it is written by the next call. A key
  # whose text is one this object already holds is refused, naming both:
  # the reader refuses a duplicate key, and the builder wrote one - a key
  # given twice, or two Strings whose bytes are not UTF-8 and are both
  # written as U+FFFD (`{"a\xFF" => 1, "a\xFE" => 2}` was written
  # `{"a\uFFFD":1,"a\uFFFD":2}`, and `JSON.parse` refused it).
  def field(name : String) : Nil
  def field(name : String, & : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  def indent=(spaces : Int32) : Nil
  def indent=(str : String) : Nil
  def initialize
  def max_nesting : Int32
  def max_nesting=(value : Int32) : Int32
  def null : Nil
  def number(val : Int32) : Nil
  def number(val : Int64) : Nil
  def number(val : UInt8) : Nil
  def number(val : UInt64) : Nil
  def number(val : Float64) : Nil
  def object(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  # Text written as it is: the caller's own JSON.
  def raw(str : String) : Nil
  def start_array : Nil
  def start_object : Nil
  def string(val : String) : Nil
  # The document's text. A container still open or no value written at all
  # is not a document, and is refused.
  def to_s : String
end

pub struct JSON
  # Text written through a `Builder` the block is handed. `indent` is a
  # count of spaces or the string one level is indented by. A block that
  # writes no value, or leaves a container open, is refused.
  def self.build(indent : String | Int32 | Nil = nil, & : (Builder -> Nil)) : String
  # The document read into `type`: `Nil`, `Bool`, `Int32`, `Int64`, `UInt8`,
  # `UInt64`, `Float64`, `String`, `Any`, a type with `derive serializable`,
  # one of those or `nil`, or an `Array` or `Hash(String, V)` of those. An
  # integer outside the type is refused, as is anything after the root
  # value.
  def self.from_json(str : String, type : T.class) : T forall T
  def initialize
  # The document as an `Any`; panics with the line and column of the first
  # thing it refuses.
  def self.parse(input : String) : Any
  # The document as an `Any`, or `nil` when it is not one.
  def self.parse?(input : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Array(T).class) : Array(T) forall T
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Hash(String, V).class) : Hash(String, V) forall V
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Nil.class) : Nil
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Bool.class) : Bool
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Int32.class) : Int32
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Int64.class) : Int64
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : UInt8.class) : UInt8
  # An integer past Int64 reaches the reader as a float that still carries
  # its digits; those are read here, so the whole UInt64 range comes back.
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : UInt64.class) : UInt64
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Float64.class) : Float64
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : String.class) : String
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : Any.class) : Any
  # A type that reads itself: the `initialize(pull)` a `derive
  # serializable` wrote. A type that admits nil reads `null` as the nil and
  # anything else as the other type (`x || raise`, as the derive asks it),
  # the way `write_or_null` writes it. That was `T.new(pull)` too, and
  # `Int32 | Nil` has no such `new`, so `JSON.from_json("5", Int32?)` and
  # `Array(Int32?)` did not build.
  def self.read_value(pull : PullParser, type : T.class) : T forall T
  # Any value `write_value` knows: `nil`, a `Bool`, a prelude integer, a
  # `Float64`, a `String`, an `Any`, an `Array` or `Hash` of those, or a type
  # that implements `ToJSON`; each of them or `nil`.
  def self.to_json(obj : T) : String forall T
  def self.write_value(val : Array(T), b : Builder) : Nil forall T
  # A String key is written as it is, and two of them are never one text.
  def self.write_value(val : Hash(String, V), b : Builder) : Nil forall V
  # Any other key is written by its `to_s`, `nil` as `"null"`, the word a
  # JSON null is, so two keys can be one text: `{nil => 1, "null" => 2}`
  # was written `{"null":1,"null":2}`, which `JSON.parse` refuses
  # ("duplicate key 'null' at line 1, column 11"). The texts written are
  # kept, and a repeat is refused, naming both keys.
  def self.write_value(val : Hash(K, V), b : Builder) : Nil forall K, V
  def self.write_value(val : Nil, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Bool, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Int32, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Int64, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : UInt8, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : UInt64, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Float64, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : String, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : Any, b : Builder) : Nil
  def self.write_value(val : T, b : Builder) : Nil forall T : ToJSON
end

# Reads a whole document into an `Any`. Like the lexer it records the first
# failure instead of panicking; `JSON.parse` and `JSON.parse?` decide what to
# do with it.
pub class Parser
  def error : String | ::Nil
  def initialize(input : String)
  def parse : Any
end

# Reads a document one event at a time: `kind` names what the reader is on,
# the `read_x` methods take it and move on. The grammar is checked as it is
# read, so a missing comma or colon is refused where it is, with a panic.
pub class PullParser
  enum Kind : Int32
    Null = 0
    Bool = 1
    Int = 2
    Float = 3
    String = 4
    BeginArray = 5
    EndArray = 6
    BeginObject = 7
    EndObject = 8
    EOF = 9
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `BeginArray`
    def begin_array? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `BeginObject`
    def begin_object? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Bool`
    def bool? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EndArray`
    def end_array? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EndObject`
    def end_object? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `EOF`
    def eof? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Float`
    def float? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Int`
    def int? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `Null`
    def null? : ::Bool
    # Returns `true` if this enum value equals `String`
    def string? : ::Bool
  end
  def bool_value : Bool
  def column_number : Int32
  def float_value : Float64
  def initialize(input : String)
  def int_value : Int64
  def kind : Kind
  def line_number : Int32
  def max_nesting : Int32
  def max_nesting=(value : Int32) : Int32
  # Reads an object, yields once at the value of `key`, and skips the rest.
  def on_key(key : String, & : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  # The number the reader is on, as it was written.
  def raw_value : String
  # The value the reader is on, as an `Any`.
  def read_any : Any
  def read_array(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil
  def read_begin_array : Nil
  def read_begin_object : Nil
  def read_bool : Bool
  def read_end_array : Nil
  def read_end_object : Nil
  # A float, or an integer read as one.
  def read_float : Float64
  def read_int : Int64
  def read_next : Kind
  def read_null : Nil
  def read_null? : Bool
  # Yields each key of the object the reader is on, with the reader at its
  # value. A key named twice is refused, as `JSON.parse` refuses it.
  def read_object(& : (String -> Nil)) : Nil
  def read_object_key : String
  # The value the reader is on, written into `json` as it is read. A number
  # is written as its own text, the text it was read from: rebuilt from the
  # Int64 or Float64 it parsed to, `12345678901234567890` came back as
  # `1.2345678901234567e+19` and `1E+2` as `100.0`, and a UInt64 id passed
  # through here did not read back as itself.
  def read_raw(json : Builder) : Nil
  # The value the reader is on, as JSON text.
  def read_raw : String
  def read_string : String
  # Passes over the value the reader is on, whole.
  def skip : Nil
  def string_value : String
end

# A type that can write itself into a `Builder`. `JSON.to_json` accepts any
# value whose type implements it, as a `derive serializable` type does.
pub trait ToJSON
  abstract def to_json(json : Builder) : Nil
end

impl ToJSON for Any
  def to_json(json : Builder) : Nil
end

module std/kernel

# Terminates the program with *status*, after writing *message* to
# standard error as a line, as `puts` writes one: a message that already
# ends in a newline gets no second one, as in the other library.
#
# The ending is `exit`'s, as the other library's `abort` is its `exit`:
# what the task deferred runs, and what a stream set to `sync = false`
# holds is written. This wrote through the runtime's own `__iyi_write` and
# ended with `__iyi_exit`, which skip both: `STDOUT.sync = false`,
# `puts "before"`, `abort "bye"` left standard output empty, a `defer`
# around the call never ran, and a line buffered on standard error before
# the message was lost.
pub def abort(message : String | ::Nil = nil, status : Int32 = 1) : NoReturn

# Repeatedly executes the block until break.
pub def loop(& : (-> Nil)) : Nil

# Inspects object to standard output followed by newline. Returns object.
pub def p(object : T) : T forall T

# Inspects each object to standard output. Returns objects tuple.
pub def p(*objects : *T) : Tuple(*T) forall T

# Pretty prints object to standard output. Returns object.
pub def pp(object : T) : T forall T

# Pretty prints each object to standard output. Returns objects tuple.
pub def pp(*objects : *T) : Tuple(*T) forall T

# Prints objects without trailing newline.
pub def print_all(*objects : *T) : Nil forall T

# Prints objects followed by a newline.
pub def puts_all(*objects : *T) : Nil forall T

surfaces.name: std/list
surfaces.stdout:
module std/list

# The store is built at construction and never handed out, so no method of this
# type can be observed to change it. That is what makes the value shareable
# under III.4.4 — every field immutable after construction — and it is why the
# constructor **copies**.
#
# The copy is not defensive habit, it is the missing borrow checker. `List`
# cannot express "I own this array now", so a caller that kept a reference to
# what it passed in could mutate the list from underneath a task holding it.
# Rust says this with ownership and pays nothing; here it costs one copy at the
# boundary, once, and it is the honest price of not having that machinery.
pub struct List(T)
  # Two lists are the same value when they hold the same elements in the same
  # order, which is the whole of what a list is. Until this method, the one
  # answering was `Object#==` (src/iyi/object.iyi:37-39), the constant
  # `false` — not even reflexive, so `list == list` was false too, and every
  # collection that asks said no: `includes?`, `index` and `uniq` all go
  # through `==`, a list could never be found in a `Hash`, and a `case` over
  # a list matched no `when`, because a `when` is `===` and `===` is `==`.
  # That is the failure object.iyi:111-120 wrote up for `Tuple`, reproduced
  # by the one type III.4.7 added for handing a value between tasks — where
  # comparing what two tasks produced is the point.
  #
  # Sizes first, because that is the cheap half of the answer. No shared-store
  # fast path like `Slice#same?`: the constructor copies, so two lists never
  # share a store, and the comparison would pay for every call to fire only
  # when a list is compared with itself.
  #
  # Restricted to `List(T)`, so a list of another element type is unequal by
  # the prelude's default rather than a compile error — the reasoning
  # object.iyi:119-120 gives for restricting `Tuple#==` to its own shape.
  def ==(other : List(T)) : Bool
  # Indexed with `[]`, because every other sequence here is — `Slice`
  # (std/slice.iyi:107), the prelude's `Array` (src/iyi/array.iyi:78) and
  # everything under `Indexable` (std/indexable.iyi:75) — and III.1.7a says a
  # name shared with Crystal means the same thing here. A negative index
  # counts from the end, so `list[-1]` is the last element; that rule was
  # already true through the backing array and unwritten, which is worse than
  # either answer.
  #
  # The out-of-range sentence is raised here rather than left to the store.
  # The array's wording is the right wording — it names the index asked for
  # and how many elements there are, and names no receiver, so there is
  # nothing in it about an array the caller never handed over — but a message
  # this type promises is this file's, not one inherited by accident from a
  # field nobody can see.
  def [](index : Int32) : T
  # The nilable partner, which is the one question `[]` cannot answer: "the
  # element there, or nothing". Without it every caller probing a list past
  # its end rewrites the bounds rule above by hand against `size`, and two
  # copies of a rule is one too many.
  def []?(index : Int32) : T | ::Nil
  protected def adopt(items : Array(T)) : Nil
  # Every operation that would change a sequence returns a new one instead, so
  # by III.1.7's convention they are all participles. The plain verbs — `push`,
  # `sort`, `reverse` — name the mutating form, and this type has none. That the
  # naming rule falls out rather than being applied is the point of having
  # settled it before any library code existed.
  #
  # Each builds its array at the size it ends with, once. `dup` then `<<`
  # copied the list, grew the copy to twice its size and handed it to the
  # constructor, which copied it a third time: an append to a list of n
  # elements wrote 4n words where n + 1 is the whole of the work.
  def appended(item : T) : List(T)
  # `at` is the name this file had before `[]`, and samples/iyi/immutable.iyi
  # is written in it. It stays, spelled out, and delegates — so both names
  # exist but only one bounds rule does.
  def at(index : Int32) : T
  def concatenated(other : List(T)) : List(T)
  def empty? : Bool
  # Hashing follows equality, or the agreement above buys nothing: a `Hash`
  # finds a key by its slot first and compares second, so two equal lists in
  # different slots are still two keys. `Object#hash` answered with the type
  # id — every `List(Int32)` in one slot, "correct and useless" in exactly
  # the way object.iyi:20-23 says of a key type that never said how it
  # hashes.
  #
  # The array's own hash, which is `Indexable#hash`'s mixing (the prelude's
  # `Array#hash`): one function, so a list and the array it was built from
  # land in the same slot.

  # the elements inside it are already inspected. Stated rather than left to
  # `Object#inspect` so it is in this module's exported surface, which is
  # what a list nested in another collection is asked for — `List[List[1]]`
  # rather than a type name — and it is how `Slice` states it too.
  def inspect : String
  # A list over an array nothing else holds: the one `appended` or
  # `concatenated` has just built. The copy above is for a caller's array,
  # which the caller still has; one made here has no other owner.
  protected def self.owning(items : Array(T)) : List(T)
  def size : Int32
  # A list prints its elements, like both of its siblings: `Slice[10, 20, 30]`
  # and the array's `[10, 20, 30]`. Inherited, it printed
  # `Std::List::List(Int32)`, which object.iyi:7-8 calls what "a value that
  # has said nothing about itself can honestly print" — and a sequence has
  # plenty to say, so the default was the type failing to answer.

  # `List["pear", "fig"]`, telling a reader the elements are strings, where
  # printing them loses that with no way to get it back.

# only reach the iterator tower through `to_a`, which copies the sequence
# the type exists to hand around without copying.
#
# A class, as `ArrayIterator` is (std/iterator.iyi): an adaptor keeps its

# `it.first(2).to_a` and then `it.to_a` gave [1, 2] and [1, 2, 3, 4] where
# an iterator over an array gives [1, 2] and [3, 4].
pub class ListIterator(T)
  def initialize(list : List(T))
  def next : T | Stop
end

impl Std::Enumerable::Enumerable for List(T) forall T
  def each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil
end

impl Std::Iterator::Iterator for ListIterator(T) forall T
end

  # hashes 204952928 and -1576659145, so a table missed one by the other.

  # so `s[-1]` is the last element; the message names the index as typed rather
  # than the wrapped one, and words it exactly as `Array#[]` and
  # `Indexable#[]` do — the same mistake reads the same way in all three.

  def []?(index : Int32) : T | ::Nil

  #

  # taken only once the end is known to be past the start, and the
  # inclusive end is added only while the count can still fit, so an end
  # near the top of `Int32` answers nil instead of overflowing.

  def bytesize : Int32

  def swap(i : Int32, j : Int32) : self
  # Returns an Array containing all elements in this slice.
  def to_a : Array(T)
  # String representation: Bytes[...] for Slice(UInt8), Slice[...] for others.
  def to_s : String
  # Raw pointer to the underlying buffer.
  def to_unsafe : Pointer(T)
  # Raw element access without bounds checks (required for Indexable).
  def unsafe_fetch(index : Int32) : T
  # Raw element write without bounds checks.
  def unsafe_put(index : Int32, value : T) : T
end

# The lazy half, which `Slice` had no way into: `std/iterator`'s header says
# a concrete collection provides its own iterator constructor and names this
# type twice as one that should, and then the only route from a slice to a
# lazy chain was `fs.to_a` — copying the whole sequence, which is the cost
# the tower exists to avoid.
#
# A class, as `ArrayIterator` is (std/iterator): an adaptor keeps its source
# by value, and a struct source was copied into it, so `it.first(2).to_a`
# and then `it.to_a` gave [1, 2] and [1, 2, 3, 4] where an array's iterator
# gives [1, 2] and [3, 4].
pub class SliceIterator(T)
  def initialize(slice : Slice(T))
  def next : T | Stop
end

impl Std::Indexable::Indexable for Slice(T) forall T
end

impl Std::Enumerable::Enumerable for Slice(T) forall T
  def each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil
end

impl Std::Iterator::Iterator for SliceIterator(T) forall T
end

module std/socket

  def initialize(b0 : UInt8, b1 : UInt8, b2 : UInt8, b3 : UInt8)
  def to_s : String
end

# Sixteen bytes in network order, held as two words: `high` is bytes 0 to
# 7. Written the RFC 5952 way - lowercase, no leading zeros, the longest
# run of two or more zero groups as `::`, the first of two equal runs -
# and an IPv4-mapped address with its dotted tail, `::ffff:192.0.2.1`.
pub struct IPv6Address
  # Byte *index*, 0 to 15.
  def [](index : Int32) : UInt8
  # The 16-bit group *index*, 0 to 7. Not `group`: that name is the task
  # group's in iyi (SPEC.md III.4.9).
  def hextet(index : Int32) : Int32
  def high : UInt64
  def initialize(high : UInt64, low : UInt64)
  def low : UInt64
  # The sixteen bytes at *bytes*, network order.
  def self.new(bytes : Pointer(UInt8)) : IPv6Address
  def to_s : String
end

pub class IyiSocket
  def self.__sys3(number : Int64, a : Int64, b : Int64, c : Int64) : Int64
  def self.__sys5(number : Int64, a : Int64, b : Int64, c : Int64, d : Int64, e : Int64) : Int64
  def self.__sys6(number : Int64, a : Int64, b : Int64, c : Int64, d : Int64, e : Int64, f : Int64) : Int64
  def self.__sys_accept(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), addrlen : Pointer(UInt32), family : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_addr_size(family : Int32) : Int64
  def self.__sys_bind(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), family : Int32) : Int32
  # Every close of a socket in this file goes through here. `__iyi_close` is
  # the descriptor close, and on Windows a socket is not a descriptor:
  # `CloseHandle` on a SOCKET releases the kernel handle and leaves Winsock's
  # half of it standing, and the graceful close that makes a peer's read
  # answer EOF rather than a reset is `closesocket`'s.
  def self.__sys_close(fd : Int32) : Nil
  # A raw syscall's negative errno, as the number.
  def self.__sys_code(result : Int64) : Int32
  def self.__sys_connect(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), family : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_connects_blocking?(family : Int32) : ::Bool
  def self.__sys_getsockname(fd : Int32, addr : Pointer(UInt8), addrlen : Pointer(UInt32)) : Int32
  def self.__sys_in_progress?(result : Int32) : ::Bool
  def self.__sys_listen(fd : Int32, backlog : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_no_sigpipe(fd : Int32) : Nil
  # `ppoll` on one descriptor for *ms* milliseconds - a timespec, or none
  # for -1 - and no signal mask. 0 when the time ran out.
  def self.__sys_poll(fd : Int32, events : Int32, ms : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_recv(fd : Int32, buf : Pointer(UInt8), len : UInt64) : Int64
  # MSG_NOSIGNAL (0x4000): a write to a connection the peer closed answers
  # EPIPE instead of killing the process with SIGPIPE.
  def self.__sys_send(fd : Int32, buf : Pointer(UInt8), len : UInt64, ms : Int32) : Int64
  # F_GETFL (3), then F_SETFL (4) with O_NONBLOCK (0x800) added.
  def self.__sys_set_nonblock(fd : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_set_reuseaddr(fd : Int32) : Int32
  # IPV6_V6ONLY (26) at IPPROTO_IPV6 (41).
  def self.__sys_set_v6only(fd : Int32) : Int32
  # SO_ERROR (4) at SOL_SOCKET (1): what a connect that was in progress
  # ended with, 0 when it went through.
  def self.__sys_sock_error(fd : Int32) : Int32
  def self.__sys_socket(family : Int32) : Int32
  # A raw syscall answers the negative errno: EAGAIN is 11, EINPROGRESS 115.
  def self.__sys_would_block?(result : Int64) : ::Bool
  def accept : IyiSocket | Cancelled | SocketError
  def self.await_readable(fd : Int32, ms : Int32 = -1) : ::Bool | Cancelled
  def self.await_writable(fd : Int32, ms : Int32 = -1) : ::Bool | Cancelled
  # A timeout as the waits take it: milliseconds, -1 for none.
  def self.bound(ms : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32
  protected def bound_path(path : String) : Nil
  # *path* with the NUL a system call reads to.
  def self.c_path(path : String) : Pointer(UInt8)
  def close : Nil
  def closed? : ::Bool
  # `localhost` is 127.0.0.1 and then ::1: a refused or unreachable
  # 127.0.0.1 is tried again at ::1. Windows names both, ::1 first, and a
  # dev server that binds `localhost` there is often on ::1 alone, where
  # a connect to 127.0.0.1 only was "connection refused". 127.0.0.1 goes
  # first because a listener here binds `localhost` there. Windows takes
  # 2 s to refuse a connect, so a ::1-only listener is reached in 2 s
  # (2017 ms measured) and a port nobody holds is refused in 4 s, not 2.
  def self.connect(host : String, port : Int32) : IyiSocket | Cancelled | SocketError
  # The stream socket listening at *path*.
  def self.connect_unix(path : String) : IyiSocket | Cancelled | SocketError
  # *host* and *port* as a message names them: an IPv6 literal in its
  # brackets, as a URL writes it. Bare, `::1:57456` was an address with
  # no port, and `ff02::1:80` another address altogether.
  def self.endpoint(host : String, port : Int32) : String
  def fd : Int32
  # The address family, the platform's number for it: an accepted
  # connection is its listener's, and on Windows the socket `AcceptEx`
  # fills in has to be made in it.
  def initialize(fd : Int32, family : Int32 = AF_INET)
  def self.listen(host : String, port : Int32, backlog : Int32 = 128) : IyiSocket
  def self.listen(port : Int32, backlog : Int32 = 128) : IyiSocket
  # A stream socket at *path*. The path must not exist: a socket file an
  # earlier run left behind is refused rather than taken over, since
  # which program owns it is not something a bind can know. `close`
  # removes the file.
  def self.listen_unix(path : String, backlog : Int32 = 128) : IyiSocket
  def local_address : String
  # The port sits at the same two bytes of a `sockaddr_in` and a
  # `sockaddr_in6`.
  def local_port : Int32
  def self.make_sockaddr_in(ip : IPv4Address, port : Int32) : Pointer(UInt8)
  # A `sockaddr_in6`: family, port, a zero flow label, the address, a zero
  # scope. The family's number and where it sits are the platform's.
  def self.make_sockaddr_in6(ip : IPv6Address, port : Int32) : Pointer(UInt8)
  # A `sockaddr_un`: the family, then the path and its NUL. The room for
  # the path is the platform's - 104 bytes on darwin, 108 elsewhere - and a
  # longer one is refused rather than cut, since a cut path is another
  # path.
  def self.make_sockaddr_un(path : String) : Pointer(UInt8)
  # Dotted-decimal IPv4 only: four octets of 0 to 255, no leading zero
  # (`"010.1.1.1"` is refused; glibc's `inet_aton` reads `010` as octal 8,
  # CVE-2021-29921, so it must not quietly be 10 here), plus `localhost`.
  # The refusal inspects the host so a stray space shows.
  def self.parse_ip(host : String) : IPv4Address
  # Eight groups of up to four hex digits, `::` once for a run of zero
  # groups, and a dotted IPv4 tail for the last two (`::ffff:1.2.3.4`). A
  # zone (`fe80::1%eth0`) is refused by name: it names an interface, and
  # this parser has no way to ask the platform which.
  def self.parse_ipv6(host : String) : IPv6Address
  def read(buffer : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError
  def read(max_bytes : Int32 = 4096) : String | Cancelled | SocketError
  # The bounds on a read's and a write's wait, in milliseconds; nil waits
  # as long as it takes.
  def read_timeout_ms : Int32 | ::Nil
  def read_timeout_ms=(ms : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def recv(buffer : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError
  def recv(max_bytes : Int32 = 4096) : String | Cancelled | SocketError
  def send(buffer : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError
  def send(contents : String) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError
  # A host and port as the address a call takes, and its family: an IPv6
  # literal bare or in brackets, anything else IPv4.
  def self.sockaddr(host : String, port : Int32) : Tuple(Pointer(UInt8), Int32)
  def to_io : IyiIO
  def to_unsafe : Int32
  def write(buffer : Pointer(UInt8), count : Int32) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError
  def write(contents : String) : Int32 | Cancelled | SocketError
  def write_timeout_ms : Int32 | ::Nil
  def write_timeout_ms=(ms : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32 | ::Nil
end

# A connection's own failure: which operation, and the platform's error
# number for why.
pub struct SocketError
  def code : Int32
  # The peer is gone: it reset the connection, or closed it and the write
  # found the pipe broken, or the connection was aborted.
  def disconnected? : ::Bool
  def initialize(operation : String, code : Int32)
  def operation : String
  def reason : String
  def refused? : ::Bool
  # A wait for the peer that ran past its socket's timeout, carrying the
  # platform's own number for it so `reason` and `timed_out?` read it as
  # they read the kernel's.
  def self.timed_out(operation : String) : SocketError
  # The peer did not answer in time: a connect the network timed out, or a
  # read or write past its socket's timeout.
  def timed_out? : ::Bool
  def unreachable? : ::Bool
end

impl Error for SocketError
  def message : String
end

module std/static_array

pub alias StaticArray = ::StaticArray

struct ::StaticArray(T, N)
  # Comparison based on lexicographical element order. Written out here: it
  # forwarded to `Slice#<=>`, which the slice module does not have, so any
  # call of this method failed to compile.
  def <=>(other : StaticArray(T, N)) : Int32
  # Equality. Returns true if corresponding elements are equal, where one
  # element type holds the other, as tuples compare (src/iyi/object.iyi).
  # Restricted to `StaticArray(T, N)`, a `StaticArray(Int32, 2)` was taken
  # for a `StaticArray(Int32?, 2)` and not back: the one equality answered
  # true one way and false the other.
  def ==(other : StaticArray(U, M)) : Bool forall U, M
  def ==(other : Object) : Bool
  # Returns the element at the given *index*. Negative indices count backward.
  def [](index : Int) : T
  # Sets the element at *index* to *value*.
  def []=(index : Int, value : T) : T
  # Returns the element at *index*, or nil if out of bounds.
  def []?(index : Int) : T | ::Nil
  def all? : Bool
  def any? : Bool
  def clone : self
  def count(item) : Int32
  def count : Int32
  # Duplicates this static array.
  def dup : self
  # Yields each element in order.
  def each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Yields each element alongside its index.
  def each_with_index(offset : Int = 0, & : (T, Int32 -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Returns true when the static array contains zero elements.
  def empty? : Bool
  # Fills *count* elements starting at *start* with *value*.
  #
  # A negative count and a start outside are refused before anything is
  # filled, as the other library and `Slice#fill` refuse them: an early
  # return for `c <= 0` came first, so `fill(7, 0, -1)` and `fill(7, 9, 0)`
  # of four elements answered the array untouched and said nothing.
  def fill(value : T, start : Int, count : Int) : self
  # Fills the entire static array with *value*.
  def fill(value : T) : self
  # Returns the first element. Raises if empty.
  def first : T
  # Returns the first element or nil if empty.
  def first? : T | ::Nil
  # Hashing follows the `==` above, mixed as `Array#hash` mixes. There was
  # only the other library's `hash(hasher)`, which no table here calls, so
  # `Object#hash` answered the type's id: every `StaticArray(Int32, 2)` was
  # one slot, and 40,000 of them took 13 s to insert where the same pairs
  # as tuples took 3 ms.
  def hash : Int32
  # Returns true if *object* is in the array.
  def includes?(object) : Bool
  # Returns the index of *object*, or nil if not found.
  def index(object, offset : Int = 0) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def inspect(io : IO) : Nil
  def inspect : String
  # Returns the last element. Raises if empty.
  def last : T
  # Returns the last element or nil if empty.
  def last? : T | ::Nil
  # Returns a new StaticArray with mapped elements.
  def map(&block : (T -> U)) : StaticArray(U, N) forall U
  # Returns a new StaticArray with mapped elements and indices.
  def map_with_index(offset : Int = 0, &block : (T, Int32 -> U)) : StaticArray(U, N) forall U
  # Creates a new StaticArray filled by invoking the block for each index.
  def self.new(& : (Int32 -> T)) : self
  # Creates a new StaticArray filled with the given value.
  def self.new(value : T) : self
  def none? : Bool
  def one? : Bool
  # Yields elements in reverse order.
  def reverse_each(& : (T -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Reverses elements in place.
  def reverse_in_place : self
  # Returns the last index of *object*, or nil if not found.
  def rindex(object, offset : Int = N - 1) : Int32 | ::Nil
  # Rotates elements in place by *n* positions. Reduced in `Int64` before it
  # is narrowed, as `index_within` and `BitArray`'s rotation count: `n.to_i`
  # panicked "arithmetic overflow" for 3000000001_i64, which rotates four
  # elements by one.
  def rotate_in_place(n : Int = 1) : self
  # Returns the size of self.
  def size : Int32
  # Returns a new sorted static array.
  def sort : StaticArray(T, N)
  def sort(&block : (T, T -> Int32)) : StaticArray(T, N)
  def sort_by(&block : (T -> _)) : StaticArray(T, N)
  # Each key computed once, by `Array#sort_in_place_by`, the merge sort of
  # key and element pairs: a comparison of `yield(a) <=> yield(b)` computed
  # it twice per comparison, 63,992,000 times for 8,000 elements.
  def sort_by_in_place(&block : (T -> _)) : self
  # Sorted by `Array#sort_in_place`, the stable merge sort, and copied
  # back. It was an insertion sort of its own, quadratic: 8,000 elements in
  # reverse order took 31,996,000 comparisons where the array's sort takes
  # under 100,000. Equal elements keep their order, as they did.
  def sort_in_place : self
  # In-place sort with custom block comparator, by the same merge sort.
  def sort_in_place(&block : (T, T -> Int32)) : self
  # Converts this static array into a heap Array.
  def to_a : Array(T)
  # The text `to_s` builds, written as `BitArray#to_s(io)` writes it. It
  # asked each element for `inspect(io)`, which no prelude type has, and
  # `IyiIO` for `<<`, which only `import std/io` gives it: `to_s(STDOUT)`
  # of a `StaticArray(Int32, 3)` did not compile, and `inspect(io)` with it.
  def to_s(io : IO) : Nil
  # Into one builder: adding each element to the text so far copied that
  # text once per element, and 10,000 elements took 1.4 s where `to_a.to_s`
  # of the same took 1 ms.
  def to_s : String
  # Returns a Slice backed by this static array.
  def to_slice : Std::Slice::Slice(T)
  # Returns a pointer to this static array's data.
  def to_unsafe : Pointer(T)
  # Returns the element at *index* without bounds checking.
  def unsafe_fetch(index : Int) : T
  # Sets the element at *index* to *value* without bounds checking.
  def unsafe_put(index : Int, value : T) : T
  def unstable_sort : StaticArray(T, N)
  def unstable_sort(&block : (T, T -> Int32)) : StaticArray(T, N)
  def unstable_sort_by(&block : (T -> _)) : StaticArray(T, N)
  def unstable_sort_by_in_place(&block : (T -> _)) : self
  def unstable_sort_in_place : self
  def unstable_sort_in_place(&block : (T, T -> Int32)) : self
  macro [](*args)
end

module std/tuple

struct ::NamedTuple(T)
  # Compares the values by name.
  #
  # Any named tuple: the keys are sorted and compared, then the values in
  # that order as tuples compare (src/iyi/object.iyi), member by member
  # where one type holds the other. `self` took `{a: 1, b: 2}` for `{a: 1,
  # b: y}` (y : Int32?) and not back, so the pair answered true one way and
  # false the other, and `case` over them did not match.
  def ==(other : NamedTuple) : Bool
  # Yields each key symbol and corresponding value.
  def each : Nil
  # Yields each value in order.
  def each_value : Nil
  # Returns true when the named tuple contains zero entries.
  def empty? : Bool
  # Returns true if the named tuple contains the given key symbol.
  #
  # The keys here and below are written with `symbolize`, never as
  # `:{{key.id}}`: a quoted key such as `"content-type"` or `"x y"` pasted
  # that way is `:content-type`, a symbol minus a call, or `:x y`, which
  # does not parse, so every one of these methods failed to compile for
  # such a key. `std/named_tuple` already wrote them this way.
  def has_key?(key : Symbol) : Bool
  # Hashing follows the `==` below, mixed as `Tuple#hash` mixes the members
  # (src/iyi/object.iyi). `Object#hash` answered the type's id, so
  # `{a: 1}` and `{a: 2}` hashed alike and 20,000 keys took 1.4 s to insert
  # where the same pairs as tuples took 1 ms. The values go in by sorted
  # key, because `==` matches by name: `{x: 1, y: 2} == {y: 2, x: 1}`, so
  # the two have to hash alike although their types list the keys in
  # another order.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize
  def inspect : String
  # Returns a Tuple containing the key symbols in order. Built with
  # `Tuple.new`, as `Tuple#map` is: for the named tuple with no keys,
  # braces are an empty hash literal.
  def keys
  # Value identity.
  def same?(other : self) : Bool
  # Number of key-value pairs in the named tuple.
  def size : Int32
  # The keys, and the values, in sorted key order: the order a type lists
  # its keys in is not part of the value.
  protected def sorted_keys
  protected def sorted_values
  # String representation: `{name: "Alice", age: 30}`. A key that is not a
  # name is quoted, as it is written: `{"content-type": "text/plain"}`.
  def to_s : String
  # Returns a Tuple containing the values in order.
  def values
end

struct ::Tuple(*T)
  # Concatenates two tuples.
  def +(other : Tuple(*U)) forall U
  # Yields each element sequentially.
  def each : Nil
  # Yields each element alongside its index.
  def each_with_index : Nil
  # Returns true when the tuple contains zero elements.
  def empty? : Bool
  # Returns the first element. Raises if empty.
  def first
  # Returns the first element, or nil if empty.
  def first?
  # Returns the last element. Raises if empty.
  def last
  # Returns the last element, or nil if empty.
  def last?
  # Returns a new Tuple with each element mapped through the block.
  #
  # This, `+`, `reverse`, and `NamedTuple#keys` and `#values` build with
  # `Tuple.new(...)`, not braces: with no members `{ }` is an empty hash
  # literal, so on the empty tuple each failed to compile with "for empty
  # hashes use '{} of KeyType => ValueType'".
  def map
  # Creates a new Tuple containing the given arguments.
  def self.new(*args : *T)
  # Reverses elements in tuple.
  def reverse
  # Value identity.
  def same?(other : self) : Bool
  # Converts the tuple into an Array typed as the union of all element types.
  # The empty tuple's is `[] of NoReturn`, the union of no types: the
  # `typeof` below had no argument there, and `Tuple.new.to_a` did not
  # compile.
  def to_a

# writers are `std/socket`'s; this module had copies, and the copies had
# drifted: its IPv6 parser read no dotted tail and its printer compressed
# only `::` and `::1`.

module std/unicode

pub struct Unicode
  # Options the case mappings take; combine them with `|`.
  enum CaseOptions : Int32
    ASCII = 1
    Turkic = 2
    Fold = 4
  end
  # The normalization forms `normalize` writes.
  enum NormalizationForm : Int32
    NFD = 0
    NFC = 1
    NFKD = 2
    NFKC = 3
  end
  def self.ascii?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The first character in titlecase and the rest in lowercase: `"ǆemal"` is
  # `"ǅemal"`, `"STRASSE"` is `"Strasse"`. The first character is still a
  # letter before the rest, so `"ΑΣ"` is `"Ας"`.
  def self.capitalize(text : String, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : String
  # The string with every maximal ill-formed subpart replaced by U+FFFD; a
  # well-formed string is answered as it is.
  def self.clean(text : String) : String
  # The bytes as a string, every maximal ill-formed subpart replaced by U+FFFD.
  def self.clean(bytes : Array(UInt8)) : String
  # Category C: Cc, Cf, Cs and Co — controls, format characters,
  # surrogates and private use.
  def self.control?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The string the UTF-16 code units spell. An unpaired surrogate is refused
  # with its index: `unpaired surrogate 0xD800 at index 3`.
  def self.decode_utf16(units : Array(UInt16)) : String
  # The string the UTF-16 code units spell, or nil at an unpaired surrogate.
  def self.decode_utf16?(units : Array(UInt16)) : String | ::Nil
  # The lowercase of one character, the simple mapping: `İ` becomes `i`
  # under Turkic rules and stays `İ` otherwise, because its full mapping is
  # `i` plus a combining dot.
  def self.downcase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : Char
  # The full lowercase mapping, one character at a time.
  def self.downcase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None, & : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil
  # The string in lowercase, full mappings, with the final sigma: a capital
  # sigma that ends a word — a cased letter before it, none after, the
  # case-ignorable characters (combining marks, format characters, modifier
  # letters and the apostrophes, periods and colons that can sit inside a
  # word) looked through — becomes `ς`, so `"ΟΔΥΣΣΕΥΣ"` is `"οδυσσευς"`.
  # With `CaseOptions::Fold` this is `foldcase`.
  def self.downcase(text : String, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : String
  # The string's UTF-16 code units: one per character up to U+FFFF, a
  # surrogate pair above.
  def self.encode_utf16(text : String) : Array(UInt16)
  # The case folding of one character where it is one code point (`Σ`, `σ`
  # and `ς` all fold to `σ`); a character whose folding is longer, like `ß`,
  # is answered unchanged — the block form and the string form fold it.
  def self.foldcase(char : Char) : Char
  # The full case folding, one character at a time: `ß` yields `s` twice.
  def self.foldcase(char : Char, & : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil
  # The string folded for comparison: `"Straße"` and `"STRASSE"` both fold
  # to `"strasse"`.
  def self.foldcase(text : String) : String
  def initialize
  # Category L: Lu, Ll, Lt, Lm and Lo.
  def self.letter?(char : Char) : Bool
  # Category Ll.
  def self.lowercase?(char : Char) : Bool
  # Category M: Mn, Mc and Me — the combining marks.
  def self.mark?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The string in the given normalization form, NFC when none is named.
  def self.normalize(text : String, form : NormalizationForm = NormalizationForm::NFC) : String
  # Whether the string is already in the given form.
  def self.normalized?(text : String, form : NormalizationForm = NormalizationForm::NFC) : Bool
  # Category N: Nd, Nl and No — digits in every script, letter numbers, and
  # the fractions and superscripts.
  def self.number?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The titlecase of one character, the simple mapping: the uppercase, except
  # for the digraphs, where `ǆ` and `Ǆ` both become `ǅ`.
  def self.titlecase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : Char
  # The full titlecase mapping, one character at a time: `ß` yields `S`, `s`.
  def self.titlecase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None, & : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil
  # Category Lt: the digraphs whose first half is capital, `ǅ` and `ᾈ`.
  def self.titlecase?(char : Char) : Bool
  # The uppercase of one character: the simple mapping, so `ß` stays `ß`
  # (its full mapping is two letters; the block form gives it).
  def self.upcase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : Char
  # The full uppercase mapping, one character at a time: `ß` yields `S` twice,
  # `ŉ` yields `ʼ` and `N`.
  def self.upcase(char : Char, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None, & : (Char -> Nil)) : Nil
  # The string in uppercase, full mappings: `"straße"` is `"STRASSE"`.
  # An ASCII-only string is the prelude's `upcase`, unless the Turkic rule
  # is on, which is a question about `i` itself.
  def self.upcase(text : String, options : CaseOptions = CaseOptions::None) : String
  # Category Lu.
  def self.uppercase?(char : Char) : Bool
  # Whether the string's bytes are well-formed UTF-8.
  def self.valid?(text : String) : Bool
  # Whether the bytes are well-formed UTF-8.
  def self.valid?(bytes : Array(UInt8)) : Bool
  # Category Z: Zs, Zl and Zp — the spaces and the line and paragraph
  # separators. Tab and newline are controls, not whitespace, here.
  def self.whitespace?(char : Char) : Bool
end

surfaces.stdout:
module std/uri

# An ordered multi-value collection representing URI query parameters
# or application/x-www-form-urlencoded form data.
pub struct Params
  # Returns the first value for *key*, or raises if not found.
  def [](key : String) : String
  # Sets the value for *key*, replacing all previous occurrences.
  def []=(key : String, value : String) : Nil
  # Returns the first value for *key*, or nil if not found.
  def []?(key : String) : String | ::Nil
  # Appends a key-value pair, preserving duplicate keys.
  def add(key : String, value : String) : Nil
  # Deletes all entries for *key*, returning the removed values or nil.
  def delete(key : String) : Array(String) | ::Nil
  # Iterates through each key-value pair.
  def each(& : (String, String -> Nil)) : Nil
  def empty? : Bool
  # Returns all values associated with *key*.
  def fetch_all(key : String) : Array(String)
  def has_key?(key : String) : Bool
  def initialize(keys : Array(String), values : Array(String))
  def initialize
  # Parses a query string into Params, decoding each name and value the
  # way the WHATWG URL standard reads `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`:
  # `+` is a space, `%XX` is the byte, and a `%` that does not start two
  # hex digits is itself. Pairs are separated by `&` and also by `;`, as
  # the other library separates them, where the standard and Python
  # 3.12's `parse_qsl` split at `&` alone: `a=1;b=2` is two pairs here and
  # one there.
  # Never a panic - the query is whatever a client sent, and `?q=100%`
  # is what browsers send for "100%". `URI.decode` stays strict: it is
  # asked of text a program made.
  def self.parse(query : String) : Params
  def size : Int32
  # Encodes parameters to application/x-www-form-urlencoded string.
  def to_s : String
end

pub class URI
  # The userinfo is compared as written, as the path is: `u%3Btype%3Da` and
  # `u;type=a` are two URIs (RFC 3986 section 2.2).
  def ==(other : URI) : Bool
  def absolute? : Bool
  # `userinfo@host:port`, the userinfo and the host written as stored.
  def authority : String | ::Nil
  def self.decode(str : String, plus_to_space : Bool = false) : String
  # Decodes `%XX` escapes (and `+` to a space when *plus_to_space*).
  # `decode?` answers nil and `decode` panics for a `%` not followed by
  # two hex digits; a multi-byte UTF-8 character encoded byte by byte
  # comes back as the character.
  def self.decode?(str : String, plus_to_space : Bool = false) : String | ::Nil
  # `+` a space and `%XX` a byte, any other `%` kept as it is: the form
  # reading `Params.parse` makes.
  protected def self.decode_form_lenient(str : String) : String
  def self.decode_www_form(str : String, plus_to_space : Bool = true) : String
  def self.decode_www_form?(str : String, plus_to_space : Bool = true) : String | ::Nil
  def self.default_port(scheme : String) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def dup : URI
  # Percent-encodes every byte that is neither unreserved nor reserved,
  # `%` among them: `"%20"` becomes `"%2520"`, and a space `"%20"` (or
  # `"+"` when *space_to_plus*, which then writes a `+` as `"%2B"`). Bytes
  # above ASCII are encoded one by one, so UTF-8 text round-trips through
  # `decode`.
  def self.encode(str : String, space_to_plus : Bool = false) : String
  # Encodes a path, keeping `/` between its segments.
  def self.encode_path(str : String) : String
  # Encodes one path segment: only unreserved bytes pass.
  def self.encode_path_segment(str : String) : String
  # Encodes a user or a password for the authority: unreserved bytes and
  # the sub-delims, which RFC 3986 section 3.2.1 lets userinfo hold, pass;
  # `:`, which separates the two, and `@`, which ends them, do not.
  def self.encode_userinfo(str : String) : String
  # Encodes a form field the application/x-www-form-urlencoded way: a
  # space is `+` unless *space_to_plus* is false, and only unreserved
  # bytes pass.
  def self.encode_www_form(str : String, space_to_plus : Bool = true) : String
  def fragment : String | ::Nil
  def fragment=(value : String | ::Nil) : String | ::Nil
  # Gen-delims: ":" / "/" / "?" / "#" / "[" / "]" / "@"
  def self.gen_delim?(byte : UInt8) : Bool
  # Hashing follows `==` (below), the eight parts mixed as a tuple's members
  # are. Without it every URI hashed to its type, so `http://a/` and
  # `https://b:8/x?y#z` hashed alike and a table of 16,000 URI keys took
  # 11.3 s to fill where the same texts as strings took 4 ms.
  def hash : Int32
  def host : String | ::Nil
  # Stored as given: an IPv6 address is written with its brackets,
  # `"[::1]"`, the way it appears in a URI, and `hostname` takes them off.
  def host=(h : String | ::Nil) : Nil
  # The host without the brackets an IPv6 address carries.
  def hostname : String | ::Nil
  def initialize(scheme : String | ::Nil = nil, host : String | ::Nil = nil, port : Int32 | ::Nil = nil, path : String = "", query : String | ::Nil = nil, user : String | ::Nil = nil, password : String | ::Nil = nil, fragment : String | ::Nil = nil)
  def normalize : URI
  def normalize_in_place : URI
  # The host in lower case and its escapes' hex digits upper-case, the
  # two rules RFC 3986 section 6.2.2.1 gives: `downcase` alone wrote
  # `%C3%A9` as `%c3%a9`, the one spelling of the escape the section
  # normalizes away from.
  protected def self.normalized_host(host : String) : String
  def opaque? : Bool
  def self.parse(raw_url : String) : URI
  # Reads *raw_url* as a URI reference. `parse?` answers nil and `parse`
  # panics with the reason for: a space or control character anywhere
  # (`space at byte 11 in "http://exa mple.com"`), a `:` before the first
  # `/`, `?` or `#` whose prefix is not a scheme (`invalid scheme "ht!tp"
  # in ...`), a `[` in the host with no `]`, a host with a byte a host
  # cannot hold, and a port that is not decimal digits or is above 65535.
  # Percent escapes are not checked here; `decode` does that.
  def self.parse?(raw_url : String) : URI | ::Nil
  def password : String | ::Nil
  def password=(password : String | ::Nil) : Nil
  def path : String
  def path=(value : String) : String
  def port : Int32 | ::Nil
  def port=(value : Int32 | ::Nil) : Int32 | ::Nil
  def query : String | ::Nil
  def query=(value : String | ::Nil) : String | ::Nil
  def query_params : Params
  def query_params=(params : Params) : Nil
  def relative? : Bool
  # Linear in the path: the input buffer of section 5.2.4 is a cursor into
  # *path*, and each step moves it past what it took. Each step sliced the
  # rest of the path into a new string, so removing the dot segments took
  # time in the square of the path's length: 132 KB of `/a/./b/../c` took
  # 12.8 s in a release build, where splitting it at its slashes took 3 ms.
  def self.remove_dot_segments(path : String) : String
  # The dot segments of a relative reference's path taken out as resolving
  # it against any base would take them: a `..` that climbs past the
  # reference's own segments stays, since only the base knows what it
  # climbs out of, and a path that ends in a dot segment names a
  # directory, so `a/..` is `./`.
  protected def self.remove_relative_dot_segments(path : String) : String
  def self.reserved?(byte : UInt8) : Bool
  # Resolves *ref* against this URI as Base URI according to RFC 3986 section 5.2.
  def resolve(ref : URI | String) : URI
  def scheme : String | ::Nil
  def scheme=(value : String | ::Nil) : String | ::Nil
  # Sub-delims: "!" / "$" / "&" / "'" / "(" / ")" / "*" / "+" / "," / ";" / "="
  def self.sub_delim?(byte : UInt8) : Bool
  def to_s : String
  # Unreserved characters: ALPHA / DIGIT / "-" / "." / "_" / "~"
  def self.unreserved?(byte : UInt8) : Bool
  def self.unwrap_ipv6(h : String) : String
  # The user and the password are kept as the reference wrote them, escapes
  # and all, and written back so: decoded by `parse` and re-encoded by
  # `authority`, `u%3Btype%3Da@h` came back `u;type=a@h`, which RFC 3986
  # section 2.2 counts a different URI, and `é` came back `%C3%A9`. The
  # getters decode; the setters and the constructor encode what they are
  # given with `encode_userinfo`.
  def user : String | ::Nil
  def user=(user : String | ::Nil) : Nil
  def userinfo : String | ::Nil
  def userinfo=(info : String | ::Nil) : Nil
  # The user and the password as written, taken as they are.
  protected def written_userinfo(user : String | ::Nil, password : String | ::Nil) : Nil
end

module std/uuid

pub struct UUID
  def ==(other : UUID) : Bool
  def bytes : Array(UInt8)
  # Hashing follows `==`: the sixteen bytes, as an array of them hashes.
  # Without it every UUID hashed to its type, so the all-zero and the all-f
  # UUIDs hashed alike and a table of 16,000 UUID keys took 2.0 s to fill
  # where the same UUIDs as strings took 5 ms.
  def hash : Int32
  # The sixteen bytes are the UUID's own, copied in here and out of
  # `bytes`, as the other library's are a value: held as the caller's
  # array, a buffer reused for the next record changed every UUID made
  # from it (`b[0] = 255_u8` after `UUID.new(b)` turned `00000000-...`
  # into `ff000000-...`), and `u.bytes[1] = 255_u8` changed a UUID that
  # was already a hash key, which its table then could not find.
  def initialize(bytes : Array(UInt8))
  def self.parse(text : String) : UUID
  protected def stored : Array(UInt8)
  def to_s : String
  def self.v4 : UUID
  def version : Int32
end

module std/xml

# *text* as character data: `&`, `<`, `>` and `\r` become references,
# every other byte is copied as it is. With *ascii*, a character past U+007F
# becomes a decimal reference as well, for a document declared US-ASCII.
pub def escape(text : String, ascii : Bool = false) : String

# *text* for inside a double-quoted attribute value: `"` and a literal tab
# or newline become references as well, so the value reads back unchanged.
# *ascii* is as for `escape`.
pub def escape_attribute(text : String, ascii : Bool = false) : String

pub def parse(xml : String, max_depth : Int32 = 256, max_entity_expansions : Int32 = 1000) : Document

pub def parse?(xml : String, max_depth : Int32 = 256, max_entity_expansions : Int32 = 1000) : Document | ::Nil

pub def unescape(text : String) : String

# The five predefined entities and character references decoded, the same
# way and with the same refusals as inside a document; nil where `unescape`
# panics.
pub def unescape?(text : String) : String | ::Nil

# Whether *cp* is a character XML 1.0 allows in a document (production [2]).
pub def xml_char?(cp : Int32) : Bool

pub struct Attribute
  def initialize(name : String, value : String, namespace_uri : String = "")
  def local_name : String
  def name : String
  # The namespace the prefix was bound to; "" for an unprefixed attribute,
  # which has no namespace, not even the default one.
  def namespace_uri : String
  def prefix : String
  # With *ascii*, as `Namespace#to_s`.
  def to_s(ascii : Bool = false) : String
  def value : String
end

pub class Document < Node
  def encoding : String
  def encoding=(value : String) : String
  def initialize(version : String = "1.0", encoding : String = "UTF-8", standalone : Bool | ::Nil = nil)
  def root : Node
  def root? : Node | ::Nil
  def standalone : Bool | ::Nil
  def standalone=(value : Bool | ::Nil) : Bool | ::Nil
  # The declaration and the document's own children are checked as the
  # reader checks them: the declaration first, the shape after each node's
  # own refusals. `version` and `encoding` were written between quotes as
  # they were, so an encoding holding a `"` closed the declaration and wrote
  # markup of its own (`Document.new(encoding: "x\" standalone=\"maybe")`),
  # and a version that is not `1.` and digits or an encoding this module
  # does not read (`ISO-8859-1`) made a document its parser refuses. So did
  # a second root element, none, text that is not white space, or a CDATA
  # section beside the root.
  def to_xml : String
  def version : String
  def version=(value : String) : String
end

pub struct Namespace
  def default? : Bool
  def initialize(prefix : String, uri : String)
  def prefix : String
  # With *ascii*, a character past U+007F in the uri is written as a
  # character reference, for a document declared US-ASCII.
  def to_s(ascii : Bool = false) : String
  def uri : String
end

pub class Node
  # The same node, by identity. It compared `id`s, and a `Document` counts
  # its own: the first `Document.new` and the first `Node.new_element`
  # were both 1, so the two were `==`, and `add_child`'s question "is this
  # node one of my ancestors" would answer yes for a stranger.
  def ==(other : Node) : Bool
  def [](name : String) : String
  def []?(name : String) : String | ::Nil
  # Moves *child* here, as the last child: a node is in one place in a
  # tree. It stayed among its old parent's children as well, so a node
  # moved from `<a>` to `<b>` was written under both and an attribute set
  # on it showed in both places; and a node added under itself or under one
  # of its own descendants made a loop that `to_xml` followed until the
  # stack ran out. That is refused, and so is a document as a child.
  def add_child(child : Node) : Node
  # The parser's own append: the child was just made, under this node, and
  # is in no list yet.
  protected def append_parsed(child : Node) : Node
  # The value of the attribute with exactly this name (`"x:attr"` is not
  # `"attr"`), or nil.
  def attribute(name : String) : String | ::Nil
  def attributes : Array(Attribute)
  def attributes=(value : Array(Attribute)) : Array(Attribute)
  # What `to_xml` refuses to write (see `serialize_node`): a name that is
  # not an XML name, and a character XML cannot hold raw or as a reference.
  protected def self.check_writable_name(name : String, what : String) : Nil
  protected def self.check_writable_text(text : String) : Nil
  def children : Array(Node)
  def children=(value : Array(Node)) : Array(Node)
  protected def collect_find_all(name : String, res : Array(Node)) : Nil
  protected def collect_text_into(parts : Array(String)) : Nil
  # A text, CDATA, comment or PI node's own text; for an element or a
  # document, the text and CDATA of every descendant, joined.
  def content : String
  def element_children : Array(Node)
  # The first descendant element whose name or local name is *name*.
  def find(name : String) : Node | ::Nil
  # Every descendant element whose name or local name is *name*, in document
  # order.
  def find_all(name : String) : Array(Node)
  def first_child : Node | ::Nil
  def first_element_child : Node | ::Nil
  # The first character past U+007F in *text*, decoded, or -1.
  protected def self.first_non_ascii(text : String) : Int32
  def has_attribute?(name : String) : Bool
  def id : Int32
  def initialize(node_type : NodeType, name : String = "", content : String = "")
  def inner_xml : String
  def last_child : Node | ::Nil
  def local_name : String
  def local_name=(value : String) : String
  def name : String
  def name=(value : String) : String
  # The namespace this element's name is in: the one its prefix is bound to,
  # or the default namespace in scope, or nil.
  def namespace : Namespace | ::Nil
  def namespace_uri : String
  def namespaces : Array(Namespace)
  def namespaces=(value : Array(Namespace)) : Array(Namespace)
  def self.new_cdata(content : String) : Node
  def self.new_comment(content : String) : Node
  def self.new_element(name : String) : Node
  def self.new_pi(target : String, content : String) : Node
  def self.new_text(content : String) : Node
  def node_type : NodeType
  def node_type=(value : NodeType) : NodeType
  def parent : Node | ::Nil
  def parent=(value : Node | ::Nil) : Node | ::Nil
  # Where this element is, as `/root/item[2]/name[1]`: each step counts
  # same-named element siblings from 1.
  def path : String
  def prefix : String
  def prefix=(value : String) : String
  # `xmlns=""` undeclares the default namespace, so a declaration with an
  # empty uri answers nil rather than being passed over.
  def resolve_default_namespace : Namespace | ::Nil
  def resolve_namespace_prefix(prefix : String) : Namespace | ::Nil
  # The root element of the tree this node is in.
  def root : Node
  # With *ascii* (a document declared US-ASCII), a character past U+007F in
  # text or an attribute value is written as a character reference: written
  # as its UTF-8 bytes, it made a document no other parser reads. A name, a
  # comment and a processing instruction have no references, so one holding
  # such a character is refused; it was written as UTF-8, and this module's
  # own parser refused the result ("byte 0xC3 is not US-ASCII, the declared
  # encoding").
  #
  # A name that is not an XML name, and a character XML cannot hold at all
  # (a C0 control but tab, newline and carriage return; U+FFFE, U+FFFF; a
  # byte that is not UTF-8), are refused here: both were written as they
  # were, so `set_attribute("k=\"1\" j", "2")` wrote two attributes and a
  # "\u0001" in text a document no parser reads. A parsed tree holds
  # neither.
  protected def serialize_node(buf : Array(String), ascii : Bool = false) : Nil
  # Sets or replaces the attribute; a prefixed name takes the namespace its
  # prefix is bound to here, "" where none is declared.
  def set_attribute(name : String, value : String) : Attribute
  def text : String
  # For a text, CDATA, comment or PI node, its own text; for an element, its
  # children are replaced by one text node with *value*.
  def text=(value : String) : Nil
  def to_s : String
  def to_xml : String
  # Nothing but XML's white space: space, tab, newline, carriage return.
  protected def self.xml_blank?(text : String) : Bool
end

pub enum NodeType : Int32
  Element = 0
  Text = 1
  CData = 2
  Comment = 3
  ProcessingInstruction = 4
  Document = 5
  def cdata? : Bool
  def pi? : Bool
end

# The parser keeps the first thing that went wrong in `error` and, once
# something has, runs its cursor to the end so every loop above it unwinds:
# `parse?` then answers nil and `parse` panics with that sentence.
pub class Parser
  # An entity's replacement text in an attribute value: a tab, newline or
  # carriage return in it is a space, as one written in the value is. One
  # that a character reference in the replacement text names is not.
  protected def self.attribute_spaces(text : String) : String
  # A value whose declared type is not CDATA, normalised further (XML 1.0,
  # 3.3.3): the spaces at either end dropped and each run of them made one.
  # Only U+0020 counts; a tab a character reference wrote stays. Values
  # were kept as written: `x="  p   q  "` of an NMTOKENS `x` read as is.
  protected def self.collapse_spaces(value : String) : String
  # The sentence the last parse failed with, or "" when it did not.
  def error : String
  # Where the first byte at or after *from* that does not begin an XML
  # character is, with the sentence it is refused with; -1 and "" when there
  # is none. Only a C0 control is caught where the text is read, so without
  # this a byte that is not UTF-8, an encoded surrogate, U+FFFE and U+FFFF
  # were read and written back, while their character references were
  # refused. With *ascii*, any byte past 0x7F is one.
  protected def self.first_bad_character(input : String, from : Int32, ascii : Bool) : Tuple(Int32, String)
  protected def self.hex4(value : Int32) : String
  def initialize(input : String, max_depth : Int32 = 256, max_expansions : Int32 = 1000)
  # Production [4a]: digits, `-`, `.`, U+00B7, the combining marks
  # U+0300-036F and U+203F-2040 continue a name without starting one.
  protected def self.name_char?(cp : Int32) : Bool
  # Whether all of *text* is one name.
  protected def self.name_shaped?(text : String) : Bool
  # XML 1.0 (fifth edition), production [4]: the characters that start a
  # name, by code point. Any byte past 0x7F was taken as starting and
  # continuing one, so `<a×b/>` read as an element named "a×b", a no-break
  # space after a name became part of it, and `<·a/>` was an element.
  protected def self.name_start?(cp : Int32) : Bool
  # `\r\n` and a lone `\r` both mean `\n` (XML 1.0, 2.11).
  protected def self.normalize_line_ends(input : String) : String
  def parse : Document
  def parse? : Document | ::Nil
  # Production [13]: space, newline, ASCII letters and digits, and
  # -'()+,./:=?;!*#@$_%
  protected def self.public_id_byte?(b : UInt8) : Bool
  # One or more digits, a dot, then digits: the version numbers the other
  # library reads (`1.0`, `1.1`, `1.`).
  protected def self.version_number?(value : String) : Bool
end

surfaces.stdout:
module std/yaml

# The value a document holds.
pub struct Any
  alias Type = Nil | Bool | Int64 | Float64 | String | Array(Any) | Hash(Any, Any)
  def !=(other : Any) : Bool
  # Structural: same kind, same value; a mapping equals a mapping with the
  # same pairs in any order. `1` and `1.0` are different values.
  def ==(other : Any) : Bool
  def [](key : Any) : Any
  def [](key : String) : Any
  # An Int32 indexes a sequence and reaches an integer key of a mapping:
  # `1: one` has the `Int64` key 1, and `doc[1]` panicked "expected a
  # sequence, not a mapping" while `[]?` and `dig?` answered nil.
  def [](index : Int32) : Any
  def []?(key : Any) : Any | ::Nil
  def []?(key : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def []?(index : Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def as_a : Array(Any)
  def as_a? : Array(Any) | ::Nil
  def as_bool : Bool
  def as_bool? : Bool | ::Nil
  # A float, or an integer widened to one.
  def as_f : Float64
  def as_f? : Float64 | ::Nil
  def as_h : Hash(Any, Any)
  def as_h? : Hash(Any, Any) | ::Nil
  def as_i : Int64
  def as_i? : Int64 | ::Nil
  def as_nil : Nil
  def as_nil? : Nil
  def as_s : String
  def as_s? : String | ::Nil
  def dig(key : String | Int32) : Any
  def dig(key : String | Int32, *rest : String | Int32) : Any
  def dig?(key : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  def dig?(key : String | Int32, *rest : String | Int32) : Any | ::Nil
  # Agrees with `==`: the same kind and value hash the same, a mapping's
  # hash does not depend on its order, and `0.0`/`-0.0` share one. A
  # sequence mixes its items as an `Array` does, a mapping sums one mixed
  # tuple hash per pair, and an integer hashes as an `Int64`. `31 * h +
  # item`, a sum of `31 * key + value` and the integer's own low bits
  # gave a 150 by 150 grid of `[i, j]` 4,769 hashes and of `{x: i, y: j}`
  # 299, `{a: 1, b: 2}` the hash of `{a: 2, b: 1}` and -1 that of 0, and
  # 40,000 such mappings took 987 ms to insert as keys; they take 19 ms.
  def hash : Int32
  def initialize(raw : Type)
  def initialize(value : Int32)
  def inspect : String
  # Which member of the union `raw` is, as one of the KIND_ constants.
  # Reference types are tested first on purpose (see the header).
  def kind : Int32
  # The name of the kind, for the sentences below.
  def kind_name : String
  def null? : Bool
  def raw : Type
  # Elements of a sequence, pairs of a mapping, characters of a string.
  def size : Int32
  # A string as itself, a number or boolean as written, nil as nothing,
  # a collection the way the prelude prints an array or a hash.
  def to_s : String
end

# Reads one stream. Every failure is recorded once in `@error` and every
# loop returns as soon as one is recorded; nothing is raised inside.
pub class Parser
  def error : String | ::Nil
  def initialize(text : String)
  # Every document in the stream, or nil with `error` set.
  def parse_all : Array(Any) | ::Nil
end

pub struct YAML
  # Block YAML for `value`, ending in a line break.
  def self.dump(value : Any) : String
  def initialize
  def self.parse(text : String) : Any
  # The first document of `text`, or nil when the stream is not YAML this
  # module reads (the whole stream is checked, not just the first
  # document). An empty stream is a null document.
  def self.parse?(text : String) : Any | ::Nil
  def self.parse_all(text : String) : Array(Any)
  def self.parse_all?(text : String) : Array(Any) | ::Nil
end
